about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Rava Ladoo Semolina Sweets
recipes.summary: Soft toasted semolina and coconut balls with sultanas, a classic Diwali sweet.
steps: Toast the semolina in 1 tbsp ghee in a wide pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until it smells nutty and turns pale gold.
Stir in the coconut, sugar, sultanas and cinnamon and cook for 2 minutes until the sugar starts to melt.
Take off the heat, add the remaining ghee, then sprinkle in the warm milk a spoonful at a time until the mix just holds when pressed.
While still warm, roll the mix into 12 balls, pressing firmly with your palms.
Cool the ladoo on a plate until firm to the touch.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 ladoo.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Coconut Barfi Squares
recipes.summary: Fudgy coconut squares set from condensed milk, a quick Diwali and Holi sweet.
steps: Line a 18cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over low heat, add the condensed milk and coconut and stir for 10 minutes until the mix thickens and pulls away from the sides.
Stir in the cinnamon, then press firmly into the tin with the back of a spoon.
Scatter over the pistachios and press them in lightly.
Cool completely, then cut into 16 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Plus 1 hour setting.
Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 7 days.

recipes.title: Baked Gujiya Coconut Pastries
recipes.summary: Crisp baked half-moon pastries filled with sweet coconut, semolina and nuts for Holi and Diwali.
steps: Mix the flour, salt and 2 tbsp ghee, add the water and knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest.
Toast the semolina in the remaining ghee for 4 minutes until fragrant, then stir in the coconut, sugar, sultanas and almonds and cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the dough thinly and cut 12 rounds about 10cm wide.
Put 1 heaped tbsp of filling on each round, brush the edge with water, fold over and press with a fork to seal.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes, turning once, until pale gold and crisp. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 pastries. Plus 20 minutes resting the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Baked Chakli Rice Flour Spirals
recipes.summary: Crunchy spiced rice and chickpea flour spirals, baked instead of deep-fried for Diwali snack boxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Mix the flours, butter, cumin, sesame and salt, then add the warm water a little at a time to make a soft smooth dough.
Fill a piping bag fitted with a star nozzle and pipe 12 spirals about 6cm wide onto the trays.
Bake for 25 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until pale gold and crisp.
Cool on the trays for 10 minutes so they crisp up.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 chakli. Baked rather than deep-fried, which also avoids hot oil.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Shankarpali Diamond Biscuits
recipes.summary: Lightly sweet, crisp baked diamonds of semolina dough, a Maharashtrian Diwali snack.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Stir the sugar into the warm milk until dissolved, then mix with the flour, semolina, ghee and salt into a stiff dough. Cover and rest.
Roll the dough 5mm thick on a floured bench and cut into 40 small diamonds with a knife.
Spread on the trays and bake for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Cool completely before storing.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 5 pieces. Plus 15 minutes resting the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Walnut Maamoul Eid Cookies
recipes.summary: Buttery semolina cookies with a cinnamon walnut filling, baked for Eid.
steps: Rub the butter into the semolina, flour and 2 tbsp sugar, add the milk and knead lightly. Cover and rest.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Mix the walnuts, extra sugar and cinnamon.
Roll the dough into 16 balls. Press a hole into each, add 1 tsp filling and pinch closed, then flatten slightly.
Press each cookie with a fork or a mould to pattern it and place on a lined tray.
Bake for 20 minutes until set and just pale gold on the base. Cool on the tray.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 30 minutes resting the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Pineapple Tarts Lunar New Year
recipes.summary: Melt-in-the-mouth buttery pastry cases with a sticky spiced pineapple jam, a Lunar New Year favourite.
steps: Simmer the pineapple, sugar, cinnamon stick and ground cloves in a small pan for 30 minutes, stirring often, until thick and jammy. Remove the spices and cool.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar, then mix in 1 egg yolk and the water to make a soft dough.
Roll into 24 balls of dough, press each into a mini muffin tin hole to make a case, then fill with 1 tsp jam.
Make little dough strips from any trimmings, lay two across each tart, and brush with the second egg yolk.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool for 10 minutes in the tin.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 tarts. Plus 20 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg yolk; the tarts are baked until cooked through.
Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Lunar New Year Almond Crisps
recipes.summary: Crisp-edged, crumbly almond cookies with a whole almond on top, traditional at Lunar New Year.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in 1 egg and the almond extract.
Stir in the flour, ground almonds and baking powder to a soft dough.
Roll into 20 balls, flatten slightly on the trays and press a whole almond into each.
Bake for 18 minutes until golden at the edges but still pale on top. Cool on the trays for 10 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Iced Lebkuchen Spiced Honey Cookies
recipes.summary: Soft German honey and spice cookies with a thin lemon glaze for Christmas.
steps: Warm the honey, brown sugar and butter in a small pan over low heat until the butter melts, then cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the flour, almonds, spices and bicarbonate of soda, then stir in the honey mix and egg to a firm dough. Chill.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Roll the dough 6mm thick and cut 20 rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Bake on lined trays for 12 minutes until puffed and set. Cool on a rack.
Stir the icing sugar and lemon juice into a thin glaze and brush over the cooled cookies. Let it set for 20 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 1 hour chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks; they soften and deepen in flavour.

recipes.title: Rough Puff Christmas Mince Pies
recipes.summary: Flaky homemade rough puff pastry cases around a spiced apple and dried fruit filling, with star lids.
steps: Simmer the apple, sultanas, raisins, sugar, extra butter, orange juice, zest and spices for 10 minutes until thick and sticky, then cool.
Mix the flour and salt, stir in the cold butter cubes, then add the iced water to a rough dough. Roll to a rectangle, fold in thirds and repeat 3 times, chilling between folds.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Roll the pastry 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds to line a 12-hole tin and 12 stars for the lids.
Fill each case with 1 heaped tbsp filling, top with a star and brush with the milk.
Bake for 22 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then move to a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pie. Plus about 45 minutes chilling between folds.
Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days, or freeze for 1 month and warm at 160°C fan before serving.

recipes.title: Calaveras Sugar Skull Cookies
recipes.summary: Vanilla cut-out cookies iced with bright decorations for Day of the Dead.
steps: Beat the butter and caster sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour to a soft dough, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Roll the dough 5mm thick and cut 24 skull or round shapes.
Bake on lined trays for 12 minutes until the edges are just golden. Cool on a rack.
Mix the icing sugar and milk into a thick icing, and decorate the cooled cookies. Leave to set for 30 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 45 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Baked Jam Doughnuts Hanukkah
recipes.summary: Soft cake-style doughnuts baked in a muffin tin, filled with apricot jam and rolled in cinnamon sugar.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and nutmeg, then whisk the milk, egg and 50g butter and fold into the dry mix until just combined.
Divide among the holes and bake for 18 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes.
Use a skewer to make a hole in the side of each, then pipe or spoon in about 2 tsp jam.
Brush each with the extra melted butter and roll in the extra sugar mixed with the cinnamon.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 doughnut.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Best the day they are made; keep up to 2 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Walnut Rugelach
recipes.summary: Flaky cream cheese pastry crescents rolled around cinnamon sugar, walnuts and apricot jam.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour, 2 tbsp sugar and salt, add the cream cheese and bring together into a dough. Divide in two, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Roll each half into a 28cm circle and spread with jam.
Mix the extra sugar, cinnamon and walnuts and scatter over the jam. Cut each circle into 8 wedges.
Roll each wedge from the wide end to the point and place point-down on lined trays.
Bake for 22 minutes until golden. Cool on the tray for 10 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 rugelach. Plus 1 hour chilling the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Almond Mandelbrot Twice-Baked Slices
recipes.summary: Crunchy twice-baked almond and cinnamon slices, ideal for dunking in a hot drink.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a tray.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, oil and vanilla, then fold in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and almonds to a sticky dough.
Shape into two logs about 25cm long and bake for 25 minutes until firm and golden.
Cool for 10 minutes, then cut each log on the diagonal into 10 slices.
Lay the slices cut-side up and bake for 15 minutes at 150°C fan (170°C conventional), turning once, until dry and crisp.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 slices.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 weeks.

recipes.title: Baked Chin Chin Nigerian Crunchies
recipes.summary: Nutmeg-scented crunchy little dough cubes, baked for a lighter version of the party snack.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Rub the butter into the flour, sugar, baking powder and nutmeg, then mix in the egg and milk to a firm dough.
Roll 5mm thick and cut into small 1.5cm cubes with a knife.
Spread over the trays in one layer and bake for 25 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and crunchy.
Cool completely on the trays so they crisp up.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 1/2 cup.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Coconut Mandazi Baked Triangles
recipes.summary: Soft, lightly sweet East African doughnut triangles made with coconut milk and baked rather than fried.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and salt, then stir in the coconut milk and egg to a soft dough.
Knead for 1 minute on a floured bench, roll 1cm thick and cut into 12 triangles.
Brush the tops with oil and place on the tray.
Bake for 18 minutes until puffed and golden. Serve warm.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 triangles.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Best the same day; reheat in a 160°C fan oven for 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Classic Victoria Sponge Squares
recipes.summary: Light butter sponge sandwiched with apricot jam and whipped cream, cut into tea-time squares.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line two 20cm square tins.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time with a spoon of the flour.
Fold in the remaining flour, milk and vanilla and divide between the tins.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden and springy to the touch, then cool completely.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, spread jam on one sponge, top with the cream and the second sponge, and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; keep filled cake chilled and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Lemon Madeira Cake
recipes.summary: A close-crumbed, buttery lemon loaf cake, the classic with a cup of tea.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Beat the butter, sugar and lemon zest for 4 minutes until pale and creamy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time with a spoon of flour each, then fold in the remaining flour, milk and lemon juice.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 55 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then on a rack. Cut into 10 slices.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store wrapped for up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Whole Orange Gluten-Free Tea Cake
recipes.summary: A moist gluten-free cake made from whole simmered oranges and ground almonds.
steps: Simmer the whole oranges in water for 60 minutes until very soft, then cool, halve and remove any pips.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm round tin.
Blend the oranges to a smooth purée, then beat in the eggs, sugar, almonds and baking powder.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 slices.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Gluten-free if the baking powder is gluten-free. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; it is better the next day.

recipes.title: Rosh Hashanah Honey Cake
recipes.summary: A tall spiced honey and orange loaf cake that stays moist for days.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, honey and oil until smooth.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and spices alternately with the orange juice until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean, covering with foil if it browns too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 20 minutes, then on a rack. Cut into 10 slices.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Wrap well and keep for up to 5 days; the flavour improves after a day.

recipes.title: Cheese and Chive Muffins
recipes.summary: Fluffy savoury muffins with melted cheese and fresh chives, great for lunchboxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, mustard powder, salt, 80g of the cheese and the chives.
Whisk the egg, milk and oil and stir into the dry mix until just combined.
Divide among the cases and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in an airtight container for 2 days or freezes for 1 month.

recipes.title: Corn and Zucchini Polenta Muffins
recipes.summary: Savoury muffins with sweetcorn, grated zucchini and a crumbly polenta texture.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, polenta, baking powder, salt, zucchini, corn and cheese.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil and fold through the dry mix until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in an airtight container for 2 days or freezes for 1 month.

recipes.title: Spinach and Feta Muffins
recipes.summary: Moist savoury muffins with spinach, salty feta and a hint of nutmeg.

items: 100g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, nutmeg, salt, spinach and feta.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil and stir into the dry mix until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in an airtight container for 2 days or freezes for 1 month.

recipes.title: Pumpkin and Sage Savoury Loaf
recipes.summary: A moist savoury loaf of pumpkin, sage and cheese, lovely sliced and buttered.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Whisk the pumpkin, eggs, oil and milk until smooth.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, salt, sage and cheese until just combined.
Pour into the tin, scatter with the pumpkin seeds and bake for 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then on a rack. Cut into 10 slices.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in the fridge for 3 days or freezes sliced for 1 month.
